limitations:
- Synthetic messages cannot cover every way people write; real-message accuracy is reported separately when available.
- Pidgin spelling is not standardised; quality varies.
- Pest and disease triage only chooses among problems listed in the context table; it is not a diagnosis. Severe or unknown cases are sent to an extension officer.
- The model must never be used to set pesticide doses without the official label; doses only come from label text placed in the context.
- Prices and conversion factors in training contexts are examples; always pass current local references.
- Reference prices in agro_unit_price come from real WFP market data (HDX); some markets stopped reporting years ago, so a reference can be several years old.
how_made:
1. Python generators (in the GitHub repo) produced messages and tables with exact labels in fr/en/pcm.
2. A test set was split off and frozen before any upload (15% random + held-out templates, towns, items).
3. Training rows went through Adaption Adaptive Data; advisory rows were created with Forge from openly licensed documents.
4. `merge_adapted.py` dropped rows with broken JSON, wrong keys, duplicates or any overlap with the test set.
sources: Cameroon - Food Prices (reference prices in agro_unit_price)
